Thanks Jamie — great context. See below for a quick, high-level benchmark based on the quantities you provided. Marissa copied for numbers and to prepare a formal quote.

High-level unit price comparison (approximate $ / 1M tokens, public list or common market comparables as of Feb 2026):
- Redwood (hosted, on-demand): $35 / 1M tokens
- Redwood (committed Dedicated, 6–12 month commit at 300–600M): $22 / 1M tokens (example committed tier)
- OpenAI (comparable model/throughput): ~$38–45 / 1M tokens (list pricing depends on model family & context length)
- Anthropic (comparable chat models): ~$40–50 / 1M tokens
- Open-model hosts (managed runners for quantized open models): ~$28–32 / 1M tokens (lower unit cost but may have tradeoffs on latency and model compatibility)

Notes & tradeoffs:
- Dedicated committed capacity reduces per-token costs significantly because of reserved GPU throughput and lower orchestration overhead. If ACME can commit to 300M+ tokens/month, dedicated pricing typically gets to the mid-$20s / 1M or lower depending on contract length and SLA.
- OpenAI/Anthropic list pricing is often higher for managed models; however they provide extremely fast time-to-market and consistent model parity. Redwood aims to be competitive on unit economics while providing production controls (KV caching, quantization profiles, routing policies) that reduce effective tokens needed in many workloads.
- For open-model hosts, costs can be lower per token but may require tradeoffs on latency, engineering overhead, and model updates. We can quantify these in the workbook.

Given your $25 / 1M target, committed Dedicated at 300–600M looks feasible to hit or beat that mark; the hosted on-demand route will be higher but provides procurement speed.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will draft a committed dedicated quote hitting ~$22 / 1M at a 12-month committed tier for 300M/month (we'll include variants at 300M and 600M).
2) We'll include a side-by-side comparison table vs OpenAI/Anthropic and a note on latency & rate-limit tradeoffs.
3) If that looks good, we can surface an MSA + SOW and a pilot plan (30-day pilot with limited commit to validate perf).

I attached an updated pricing workbook and SOC2 questionnaire.
